answer: The mirror multiplier is published, charged in karst, and pigment lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1353 identities would post 2769 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
